_doc: eco enforcement hooks - example configuration.
The hooks ship INERT. Nothing in this directory changes Claude Code's behaviour
until this file exists at <config-dir>/eco-hooks.json. Its existence is the opt-in.
<config-dir> is $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set, otherwise ~/.claude
(%USERPROFILE%\.claude on Windows). $ECO_HOOKS_CONFIG overrides the whole path.
Install:  cp scripts/hooks/config.example.json ~/.claude/eco-hooks.json
Verify:   node scripts/hooks/status.mjs
Disable:  delete the file, or set "enabled": false below.
Every value here is the built-in default, so copying this file unchanged turns on
all four hooks at their default thresholds. Keys beginning with _ are ignored.
A malformed value falls back to its default; a malformed file disables the hooks
entirely rather than breaking a tool call.
PostToolUse on Bash. Collapses repeated/progress lines, keeps a head and a tail,
and appends a marker stating exactly how many lines were removed and where the
untrimmed output was saved.
bashOutputTrim._floorBytes: Output at or below this many bytes is never touched.
bashOutputTrim._headLines: Lines kept from the start of the output.
bashOutputTrim._tailLines: Lines kept from the end of the output.
bashOutputTrim._collapseRepeats: Collapse runs of near-identical lines before the head/tail cut.
bashOutputTrim._repeatThreshold: Run length that triggers a collapse. Digits are normalised first, so a progress counter counts as one repeated line. Minimum 2.
bashOutputTrim._keepFullOutput: Write the untrimmed output to a file so the removed lines stay recoverable. With this off, the marker says the output was not saved.
bashOutputTrim._cacheDir: Where to keep those files. Empty string means <os temp dir>/eco-hooks.
bashOutputTrim._cacheMaxAgeHours: Cached outputs older than this are deleted on the next trim. 0 disables pruning.
bashOutputTrim._errorSignatures: Case-sensitive, multiline regexes. If ANY of them match anywhere in the output, the output is left completely alone - a truncated stack trace is worse than a long one. Narrow this list if it exempts too much; a pattern that fails to compile is skipped, not fatal.

_doc: PreToolUse on Write. Denies a Write that would overwrite an existing file larger
than the threshold, naming the file and its size and pointing at Edit. New files
and small files are never blocked.
writeGuard._maxExistingBytes: Existing files larger than this may not be rewritten with Write. 16384 is about 4k output tokens of re-emitted text.
writeGuard._exemptPatterns: Plain substrings (not regexes) of the resolved absolute path that are always allowed, e.g. "/generated/" or "dist".

_doc: PreToolUse on Read injects a limit when a long file is read without one.
PostToolUse on Read appends the file's true line count when the read was windowed,
so the model knows it has not seen the whole file.
readWindow._maxLines: Files with more lines than this get a limit injected when the call has none.
readWindow._annotate: Append the true line count after a windowed Read.
readWindow._maxScanBytes: Stop counting newlines after this many bytes. Past it the reported count is labelled 'at least N', never presented as exact.
readWindow._permissionDecision: "none" (default) sends updatedInput on its own, leaving your permission rules in charge. "allow" pairs it with an explicit allow, which some Claude Code builds require for updatedInput to take effect - but that bypasses permission rules for this tool. "ask" escalates to you.

_doc: PreToolUse on Grep. Sets head_limit when output_mode is "content" and no
head_limit was given. Other output modes and explicit limits are untouched.
grepLimit._defaultHeadLimit: Injected head_limit. Grep's own default for content mode is 250. Set 0 to disable this hook.
